summary.oneLiner: Research-driven agrochemical company specializing in the development and manufacturing of insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and plant growth regulators in India, with over 40 years of industry experience.
summary.business: GSP Crop Science develops, manufactures, supplies and distributes crop-protection Formulations (products of active ingredients plus additives) and Technicals (concentrated active ingredients) across insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and plant growth regulators. It sells domestically on a B-to-B and B-to-C basis under brands such as SLR 525, Platform, PCT-410, All Rounder, Afford, Aurthor, Liger, Raavan, Element, Runway and Fighter, and internationally on a B-to-B basis to customers in 37 countries.

currentContext.expansion: The company is expanding its international footprint into the Latin American market, having acquired GSP Agroquimica Do Brasil LTDA in Brazil in 2023, and is in the process of incorporating a subsidiary in Uruguay (subject to approvals). It operates five manufacturing facilities across Gujarat and Jammu & Kashmir with aggregate installed capacity of 15,120 MTPA Technicals, 43,672 MTPA Formulations and 5,400 MTPA Intermediates.

one-line thesis: GSP Crop Science is successfully pivoting from generic technicals to high-margin patented combinations (now 20% of revenue, targeting 40-50%), driving a 32% YoY EBITDA growth in 9MFY26 despite raw material inflation. The company's ability to fully pass through 10-15% cost increases in B2B channels and its focus on irrigation-independent crops (paddy) mitigates near-term macro risks like El Nino and Middle East conflicts.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,114 Cr (9MFY26); EBITDA: INR 153 Cr (+32% YoY), Margin ~13.7%; PAT: INR 75 Cr (reported, includes INR 4.5 Cr exceptional provision for labor wage code), Normalized PAT ~INR 79.5 Cr; Order Book: Not disclosed (seasonal B2C/B2B model); Net Debt: Not disclosed.
guidance: Revenue: Targeting 5-7% higher growth than historical CAGR over next 3 years; Margin: Patented products carry 20-25% premium over generics (55-60% gross margin vs 35-40%); Order Inflow: Strong acceptance of new insecticide/fungicide mix in paddy; Capex: No major greenfield capex, focusing on debottlenecking existing facilities.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Business operates on seasonal sales cycles with 45 days of imported inventory coverage.
segment / subsidiary detail: Domestic B2B (40%): High price elasticity, immediate cost pass-through. Domestic B2C (40%): 5,000 distributors, 24 C&F locations, slight lag in price realization. Exports (20%): 37 countries, B2B model, prices passed through globally.
growth verticals / optionality: Patented portfolio expansion (12 commercialized, 1-2 launches/year, targeting 40-50% revenue contribution in 3 years); Brazil subsidiary for exporting patented formulations; Nutrition products benefiting from fertilizer shortages.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin differential: Patented (55-60%) vs Generics (35-40%). Cost inflation (crude, logistics doubled from China) fully passed through in B2B (10-15% price hike); B2C seeing phased acceptance from April 1.
capex / expansion: Utilization: Technical plants 70-75% (peak 90%), Formulations 30-40% (seasonal). Peak capacity revenue potential: INR 1,900-2,000 Cr. Strategy focuses on debottlenecking rather than new capacity for next 3 years.
capital allocation: R&D investment for 5-year product development cycle; Registration costs (5 years/product); Working capital for 45-day import inventory.
risks & watch-items: El Nino impact on non-irrigated crops (mitigated by paddy focus); Prolonged Middle East conflict disrupting shipping beyond 1 month; Raw material availability from China; Regulatory delays in product registration.
management quality / tone: Confident on pricing power and product differentiation; Pragmatic about supply chain lags; Strategic focus on long-term R&D pipeline over rapid launch volume.
non-obvious takeaways: Co-marketing strategy involves white-labeling patented products for major peers (Rallis, Sumitomo, Mankind Agri, Chambal Fertilizers) to scale reach without incremental marketing spend; Nutrition products seeing surge due to fertilizer scarcity acting as a hedge.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.
